svg.title: The clock moves when the curve moves out
svg.desc: Two graphs compare the same polar-angle coordinates at offset 25. Dashed curves are tangent-line heights; solid curves are radial deficits of the plane drawing. At the front triple, parameter zero, the solid curves form a triangle. They meet together later, at parameter about 0.07001970943. The three plane visits then have different normal angles, about 0.074448, zero, and minus 0.074448 radians. A lower graph shows distance times the triple parameter approaching 225 over 128. A narrow shaded band encloses the exact local value between a cubic approximation and that approximation plus 40 over distance to the fifth power, for every distance at least 25. Graph axes use different units. Rounded paths illustrate separate rational proofs; no whole-movie offset threshold is claimed.

g.text: The clock moves when the curve moves out.
Compare the two pictures at the same polar angle. Their meetings happen at different times.
Plane radial deficit D = M − radius
δ = 0 · the plane still has a small triangle
One polar direction, three normal directions: +0.074448… 0 −0.074448… radians.
Multiply the meeting time by the distance.
Mδ approaches 225/128. The blue band is an exact bound; the gold path is numerical.
